dedupe_keys.name: world bank global financial development database gfdd

description: The Global Financial Development Database (GFDD) is a World Bank dataset of 108 indicators of financial system characteristics for 214 economies, organised in a 4x2 framework that measures the depth, access, efficiency and stability of financial institutions, such as banks and insurers, and of financial markets, such as stock and bond markets. It is produced by the World Bank alongside its Global Financial Development Report. Coverage is annual from 1960; the latest release, September 2022, holds data to 2021 and changed the method of some indicators, as the metadata explain. The data come as a single Excel file, free, with earlier versions back to November 2013. Caveats: the World Bank states it is not responsible for the quality of the reported information and points users to the original providers, the page read gives no licence, and no release since 2022 is shown, so it is marked stale. For simulation it gives cross-country baseline measures of banking depth and stability used to parameterise financial contagion and resilience models and to compare how exposed economies are to shocks that disrupt payments and credit for infrastructure. It is related to the FRED record in this catalogue, which holds higher-frequency financial series for the United States.
